questions.question_text: Insurance works on the principle that a large number of persons contribute small premiums to a common pool from which the few who suffer losses are compensated. This is called:
options: Risk pooling, in which the loss of a few is shared by all the insured
Risk elimination, in which the chance of every loss is removed completely
Risk avoidance, in which the insured persons stop the risky activity
Risk retention, in which every insured person bears his own loss

questions.question_text: A contract of insurance is based on "utmost good faith" (uberrima fides), which means that the:
options: Proposer is free to hide facts that are not asked in the proposal form
Proposer must disclose all the material facts truthfully to the insurer
Insurer may cancel the policy at any time without giving a reason
Insurer must disclose all its profits to the proposer of the policy

questions.question_text: A person buys a policy on the life of a stranger who has no relation to him. The policy is not valid because the buyer lacks:
options: The right of subrogation against the insurer
Utmost good faith towards the insurer
The proximate cause of the loss insured
Insurable interest in the life insured

questions.question_text: A man insures his own house for Rs 10 lakh, whereas its value is Rs 6 lakh. After a total loss by fire, the insurer will pay at most:
options: Rs 10 lakh, the sum insured, whatever the actual loss
Rs 4 lakh, the difference between the two values
Rs 16 lakh, the sum of the value and the sum insured
Rs 6 lakh, the actual loss, by the principle of indemnity

questions.question_text: The principle of indemnity applies to:
options: Life insurance, but not to the fire and motor insurance
Only to the personal accident insurance of the persons
Only to the insurance of the lives of the children
Fire and motor insurance, but not to the life insurance

questions.question_text: After paying the claim for a car damaged by a negligent third party, the insurer can recover the amount from the third party. This right is called:
options: Average
Assignment
Contribution
Subrogation
questions.explanation: Takes the place of the insured.

questions.question_text: A building is insured with two insurers for Rs 5 lakh each. It suffers a loss of Rs 4 lakh. Each insurer will pay Rs 2 lakh by the principle of:
options: Subrogation
Proximate cause
Utmost good faith
Contribution

questions.question_text: The "proximate cause" principle states that the insurer is liable for a loss if:
options: The loss is caused by a peril which is excluded in the policy
The nearest or dominant cause of the loss is an insured peril
The loss is caused by the intentional act of the insured
Any remote cause of the loss is an insured peril

questions.question_text: The amount that the policyholder pays periodically to the insurer for the cover is the:
options: Sum assured
Bonus
Premium
Surrender value

questions.question_text: The sum assured in a life insurance policy is the:
options: Amount of the tax payable on the policy by the insured
Amount of the commission paid to the agent by the insurer
Amount payable on death or maturity as per the policy
Amount paid by the policyholder as premium every year

questions.question_text: A term insurance plan is a:
options: Pension plan which pays an income after the retirement of the insured
Pure protection plan which pays only if the insured dies during the term
Investment plan whose value depends on the stock market
Savings plan which pays a lump sum on survival at the end of the term

questions.question_text: Compared with an endowment plan, a term plan of the same sum assured has:
options: The same premium, without any death benefit
The same premium, with a maturity benefit
A much higher premium, with a maturity benefit
A much lower premium, but no maturity benefit

questions.question_text: An endowment policy pays the sum assured:
options: Only on the surrender of the policy after the first year
On the maturity if the insured survives, or on death if it occurs earlier
Only on the death of the insured during the policy term
Only if the insured meets with an accident during the term

questions.question_text: A whole life policy remains in force until:
options: The insured attains the age of 60 years
A fixed number of years such as 20 years from the date of issue
The death of the insured, when the sum assured is paid
The insured stops paying the premium for a year

questions.question_text: A money-back policy differs from an endowment plan in that it:
options: Pays a part of the sum assured at regular intervals during the term
Pays the premium back at the end of the term only
Pays the entire sum assured only on the death of the insured
Pays nothing if the insured survives till the end of the term

questions.question_text: In a Unit Linked Insurance Plan, the premium is:
options: Fully used for life cover with no part of it invested at all
Partly used for life cover and partly invested in market-linked funds
Fully invested in government securities with no life cover
Fully returned at the end of the term with a fixed interest

questions.question_text: The returns on a ULIP are:
options: Guaranteed by the insurer at the time of the purchase
Fixed at 12% a year by the regulator for all the policyholders
Not guaranteed, as they depend on the performance of the chosen fund
Guaranteed by the government of India for the entire term

questions.question_text: The lock-in period for a ULIP is:
options: 5 years
3 years
10 years
1 year

questions.question_text: If a policyholder stops paying premiums in a traditional plan after paying for at least the minimum years, the policy may become a:
options: Lapsed policy, with the full sum assured
Paid-up policy, with a reduced sum assured
Surrendered policy, with the full premiums refunded
Matured policy, with the full sum assured

questions.question_text: The free look period of a life insurance policy allows the policyholder to:
options: Return the policy within 15 days if he is not satisfied with the terms
Return the policy after 5 years and get all premiums back
Change the nominee of the policy only after 10 years
Borrow against the policy right from the very first day

questions.question_text: The grace period for payment of the annual premium of a life policy is generally:
options: 90 days
7 days
180 days
30 days

questions.question_text: A lapsed policy can be restored through:
options: Assignment, by giving the policy over to another person
Surrender, by claiming the money paid so far from the insurer
Revival, by paying the arrears of premium with interest in the allowed period
Maturity, by waiting for the term of the policy to come to an end

questions.question_text: A nominee under a life insurance policy is the person who:
options: Verifies the health status of the policyholder
Receives the claim amount on the death of the policyholder
Pays the premium for the policyholder every year
Sells the policy to the policyholder as an agent

questions.question_text: A policy loan can be taken by the policyholder against:
options: The premiums yet to be paid
The sum assured of the policy
The surrender value of the policy
The bonus declared in the future

questions.question_text: Surrender value of a policy is the:
options: Amount paid to the policyholder if he terminates the policy before maturity
Amount paid to the agent for selling the policy
Amount paid to the nominee on the death of the policyholder
Amount payable by the policyholder to revive the policy

questions.question_text: Bonus in a participating life policy is:
options: A share in the surplus of the insurer, added to the sum assured
A discount on the premium given on the timely payment
A fixed amount given by the government for the first year
A commission paid to the agent for each policy sold

questions.question_text: A person aged 30 buys a Rs 1 crore term cover for 30 years. The premium will generally be lower than for a person aged 45 because:
options: The sum assured is reduced for the younger person
The insurer pays no commission to the agent for the young
The risk of death in the term is lower for the younger person
The young person pays the tax at a lower rate on the premium

questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT usually affect the premium for a life policy?
options: The age of the proposer
The colour of the policy document
The term and the sum assured
The health and habits of the proposer

questions.question_text: A person who smokes will normally pay:
options: A higher premium than a non-smoker of the same age
No premium for the first five years of the policy
A lower premium than a non-smoker of the same age
The same premium as a non-smoker of the same age

questions.question_text: Underwriting in insurance means:
options: The process of settling a claim after the loss has occurred
The process of printing the policy document for the insured
The process of assessing the risk and deciding the terms and the premium
The process of selling the policy to a large number of persons

questions.question_text: The process of the insurer transferring a part of the risk to another insurer is called:
options: Reinsurance
Co-insurance
Subrogation
Underwriting

questions.question_text: A "claim" in insurance is:
options: A request made by the insured to the insurer for payment under the policy
A request made by the regulator to the insurer for the data
A request made by the agent to the insurer for the commission
A request made by the insurer to the insured for the premium

questions.question_text: To claim for a motor accident, the insured should first:
options: Repair the vehicle and then inform the insurer about the loss
Sell the vehicle and then claim the sale value
Wait for a year and then inform the insurer
Inform the insurer promptly and file a police report where it is required

questions.question_text: Third-party insurance for a motor vehicle in India is:
options: Optional for private cars and compulsory for the bikes
Compulsory only for the commercial vehicles
Not available for the two-wheelers
Compulsory under the Motor Vehicles Act

questions.question_text: A comprehensive motor policy covers:
options: Damage to the own vehicle along with the third-party liability
Only the theft of the vehicle and nothing else
Only the damage to the third party and no damage to the own vehicle
Only the fuel and the maintenance of the vehicle

questions.question_text: No Claim Bonus (NCB) in motor insurance is:
options: A refund of the third-party premium to the insured
A discount on the own-damage premium for the claim-free years
An extra premium for every year without a claim
A penalty on the insured who has made a claim

questions.question_text: The Insured Declared Value (IDV) of a car is:
options: The cost of the insurance premium for the year
The original price of the vehicle, which stays the same
The current market value of the vehicle, which falls with the age
The price at which the vehicle can be sold as scrap

questions.question_text: Health insurance policies in India which pay the actual hospital bills up to the sum insured are called:
options: Indemnity or mediclaim policies
Personal accident policies
Fixed benefit or hospital cash policies
Critical illness policies

questions.question_text: A critical illness plan pays:
options: The premium paid, with interest, if the insured dies
A lump sum on the diagnosis of a listed illness, whatever the bills
A fixed sum on every visit made by the insured to a doctor
Only the hospital bills, up to the sum insured of the policy

questions.question_text: Cashless hospitalisation means that:
options: The patient is treated in a government hospital free of cost
The hospital waives the bill if the patient holds any policy
The patient pays nothing to the hospital under any circumstance
The insurer pays the bill directly to the network hospital as per the policy terms

questions.question_text: A TPA (Third Party Administrator) in health insurance:
options: Audits the accounts of the insurer on behalf of the regulator
Facilitates claim processing between the insurer, hospital and policyholder
Regulates the premiums which are charged by the insurers
Sells the policies as a registered agent of the insurer

questions.question_text: A "waiting period" in a health policy for a pre-existing disease means that:
options: The disease is not covered until the specified period passes
The disease is never covered under any health policy
The disease is covered only if the premium is doubled
The disease is covered from the very first day of the policy

questions.question_text: Co-payment in a health policy means:
options: The insurer bears the whole claim in all cases
The government pays a part of the premium in all cases
The policyholder bears a fixed percentage of every claim
The hospital bears a part of the claim in all cases

questions.question_text: Room rent capping in a health policy can result in:
options: Payment of the full bill whatever the room taken
Payment of the room rent to the hospital in advance
Payment of a bonus to the patient who takes a cheaper room
A proportionate reduction of the other charges if a higher room is taken

questions.question_text: Sub-limits in a health policy are:
options: Limits on the number of policies that a person can buy
Limits on the premium which a person can pay for a policy
Limits on payment for specific treatments within the sum insured
Limits on the age at which a person can buy a policy

questions.question_text: Portability of a health policy allows the policyholder to:
options: Switch to another insurer and carry forward the waiting-period credits
Take the policy abroad without informing the insurer
Pass the policy to a friend after paying a transfer fee
Receive a refund of the entire premium on the switch

questions.question_text: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides:
options: A health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year to eligible poor families
A pension of Rs 5,000 per month to all senior citizens
A term cover of Rs 2 lakh to all the farmers of the country
A cover of Rs 50 lakh per person to the salaried employees

questions.question_text: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana provides:
options: A cover for the loss of a vehicle in case of a road accident
A cover for the loss of crops of the farmers due to a drought
A health cover of Rs 5 lakh against the hospital bills of the family
A renewable one-year life cover of Rs 2 lakh on death for a low premium

questions.question_text: The Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana provides:
options: A pension for the workers in the unorganised sector
A cover for the crops of the farmers against a natural calamity
A cover for the hospital expenses of the senior citizens
An accident death or disability cover of Rs 2 lakh for a small premium

questions.question_text: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is meant to:
options: Give a life cover to the farmers on their death during the year
Protect farmers from crop loss due to calamities, pests and diseases
Give loans to the farmers for the purchase of tractors
Give a pension to the farmers on their retirement from farming

questions.question_text: Which regulator supervises the insurance sector in India?
options: RBI
SEBI
IRDAI
PFRDA

questions.question_text: The IRDAI was established under the:
options: Insurance Act, 1938 alone
IRDA Act, 1999
Banking Regulation Act, 1949
SEBI Act, 1992

questions.question_text: The Life Insurance Corporation of India was formed in:
options: 1956 by nationalising the life insurance business
1969 by the merger of the postal services
1991 by the economic reforms
1947 by the merger of the banks

questions.question_text: A person who sells insurance policies on behalf of one insurer and earns a commission is a(n):
options: Insurance agent
Insurance ombudsman
Insurance surveyor
Insurance actuary

questions.question_text: An insurance surveyor is a person who:
options: Assesses the extent and cause of a loss for the purpose of the claim
Hears the complaints of the policyholders against the insurers
Sells the policies to the customers and earns the commission
Decides the premium rates of the policies of the insurer

questions.question_text: An actuary in an insurance company:
options: Hears the appeals of the policyholders against the insurer
Calculates the premiums, reserves and risks using statistics
Inspects the damaged property of the policyholders
Sells the policies to the individuals and the groups

questions.question_text: The Insurance Ombudsman deals with:
options: Complaints of the agents against the policyholders of the insurer
Complaints of the insurers against the regulator of insurance
Complaints of the banks against the borrowers of the bank
Complaints of policyholders against insurers and intermediaries

questions.question_text: An insurance claim for a life policy is more likely to be repudiated (rejected) if:
options: The nominee submitted the claim form with all the documents
The proposer paid every premium before the due date
The proposer had concealed a material fact such as a serious disease
The death occurred after the policy had been in force for 5 years

questions.question_text: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, after the policy has been in force for three years, a claim cannot be repudiated on the ground of:
options: Non-payment of the premium due on the policy
Misstatement, unless it is proved to be fraudulent
Suicide of the life assured in the first year
Death of the life assured within the policy period

questions.question_text: The "sum assured" of a term policy of Rs 50 lakh with a rider for accidental death of Rs 25 lakh pays on the accidental death:
options: Rs 50 lakh only
Rs 75 lakh in total
Rs 1.25 crore in total
Rs 25 lakh only

questions.question_text: A rider in a life policy is:
options: A clause that excludes the cover for a specified cause
A nominee of the policy appointed by the insured
A document to be signed by the agent of the insurer
An optional additional benefit available for an extra premium

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common exclusion in a health insurance policy?
options: Hospitalisation due to an accident
Surgery for an appendicitis
Hospitalisation due to a dengue fever
Cosmetic surgery undertaken without a medical need

questions.question_text: A person pays an annual premium of Rs 25,000 for a health policy under the old regime. Under Section 80D, the maximum deduction for a person below 60 (self, spouse and children) is:
options: Rs 1 lakh

questions.question_text: A person below 60 pays Rs 20,000 as health premium for self and Rs 40,000 for senior-citizen parents. The total 80D deduction under the old regime (limits Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000) is:
The maturity proceeds of a life insurance policy are generally exempt under Section 10(10D) provided the premium does not exceed a specified percentage of the sum assured, which is:
options: 25% of the sum assured for all the policies
5% of the sum assured for all the policies
50% of the sum assured for all the policies
10% of the sum assured for policies issued after 2012

questions.question_text: The premium paid on a life insurance policy can be claimed as a deduction under the old regime in:
options: Section 80G, as it is a donation
Section 80C, subject to the overall limit
Section 24, as it is an interest
Section 80D, as it is a health premium

questions.question_text: General insurance includes:
options: Whole life and endowment policies
Fire, marine, motor and health insurance
Term and money-back plans
Pension and annuity plans

questions.question_text: The life insurance business and the general insurance business are required to be conducted by:
options: Separate companies
The cooperative societies only
The same company in a single account
The banks only

questions.question_text: Marine insurance covers:
options: Only the loss of the ports and the harbours
The loss of goods in transit by sea, the ship and the freight
Only the loss of the passengers travelling on the ship
Only the loss of the fishing nets of the fishermen

questions.question_text: A fire policy normally covers the loss of:
options: Property by the war and the nuclear risk
Property by fire and allied perils such as lightning
Property by the wear and tear of the use
Property by theft and burglary only

questions.question_text: The average clause in a fire policy means that, if the property is under-insured, the claim is:
options: Reduced in the proportion of the sum insured to the value
Paid at double the amount of the loss suffered
Rejected in all the cases without any payment
Paid in full up to the actual loss suffered

questions.question_text: A property worth Rs 10 lakh is insured for Rs 5 lakh with an average clause. A loss of Rs 4 lakh occurs. The claim payable is:
options: Rs 4 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 2 lakh

questions.question_text: In a life insurance policy of 20 years with a premium of Rs 50,000 a year, the total premiums paid in the term are:
options: Rs 1 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 20 lakh
Rs 10 lakh

questions.question_text: A term plan of Rs 1 crore costs Rs 15,000 a year. The premium per Rs 1,000 of cover is:
options: Rs 150
Rs 15

questions.question_text: A family with annual expenses of Rs 6 lakh and 15 years of need wants a cover. A rough human life value approach suggests a cover of about:
options: Rs 9 lakh
Rs 90 lakh
Rs 6 lakh
Rs 15 lakh

questions.question_text: A thumb rule often suggested for the term cover is:
options: About 10 to 15 times the annual income
About 50 times the monthly income
About 2 times the annual income
About 1 time the annual income

questions.question_text: The first-year charges in a ULIP are high because it has:
options: No charges at all in the initial years of the policy
A guaranteed return on the funds chosen by the policyholder
Premium allocation, mortality and admin charges deducted at the start
A free insurance cover for the first year of the policy

questions.question_text: Net Asset Value (NAV) in a ULIP is:
options: The price per unit of the fund at which units are bought or redeemed
The total premium paid by the policyholder in the year
The charge for the mortality cover
The sum assured of the policy

questions.question_text: Switching in a ULIP means:
options: Changing the policy from one insurer to another insurer
Changing the nominee of the policy
Moving the money from one fund to another within the same policy
Changing the premium payment date

questions.question_text: The Insurance Act, 1938 requires an insurer to maintain:
options: Only equity shares in its investments for higher returns
No reserves at all, as the premiums are received in advance
An adequate solvency margin so that it can pay the claims
Only cash and no investments in its books of accounts

questions.question_text: Which of these is TRUE about the premium of a term plan with a "return of premium" option?
options: The premium is not payable
The premium is the same as that of the pure term plan
The premium is higher than that of the pure term plan
The premium is lower than that of the pure term plan

questions.question_text: A senior citizen is likely to find that a health policy has:
options: A lower premium and fewer restrictions than for a young person
The same premium and the same restrictions as for a young person
A higher premium and more restrictions than for a young person
No premium and no restrictions

questions.question_text: An "umbrella" or "top-up" health cover is useful to:
options: Reduce the cover below the deductible limit
Avoid the claim process
Increase the cover cheaply above a deductible limit
Avoid the paying of any premium

questions.question_text: A deductible in a health policy is:
options: The amount of the premium refunded by the insurer to the insured
The amount of the commission paid to the agent for the policy
The amount of the claim which the insured must bear before the insurer pays
The amount of the bonus added to the sum insured every year
questions.explanation: Initial amount borne by the insured.

questions.question_text: Group health insurance given by an employer to the employees is:
options: Costlier per head, and it continues for the whole life
Available only to the senior management of the company
Available only to the self-employed persons in the country
Cheaper per head, but it may end when the employee leaves the job

questions.question_text: The best time to buy a health policy is:
options: Just before a planned surgery that the person wants to undergo
When young and healthy, as the premium is lower and waiting periods pass early
After the age of 70 years when the need for it is the highest
After a serious illness has been diagnosed in the family

questions.question_text: A person whose claim was repudiated by the insurer wrongly should first:
options: Approach the insurer's grievance cell and then the Insurance Ombudsman
Stop paying the premium on the other policies
Ignore the matter as the insurer cannot be challenged
Cancel all the other policies in the name of the person

questions.question_text: The Insurance Ombudsman can award compensation up to:
options: Rs 5 crore, as per the rules in force
Rs 30 lakh, as per the rules in force
Any unlimited amount, as per the rules in force
Rs 1,000, as per the rules in force

questions.question_text: A valid reason to avoid buying insurance as an investment is that:
options: The cover is not paid on the death of the person insured
The premium is not deductible under any section of the Income-tax Act
The returns are generally lower than market-linked options and the lock-in is long
The insurer is not regulated by any authority in the country

questions.question_text: Buying insurance for the protection and investing separately is described as:
options: "Buy whole life and stop investing"
"Buy endowment and ignore the term"
"Buy term and invest the rest"
"Buy no insurance and rely on the savings"

questions.question_text: A pure risk is one where the possible outcome is:
options: Only a gain, with no chance of a loss
Either a gain or a loss, with equal chances
Neither a gain nor a loss
Either a loss or no loss, with no chance of a gain

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an insurable risk?
options: Loss in a business due to a fall in the price of the product
Loss in a share market due to a price fall
Loss on a bet on a cricket match
Loss of a house in a fire

questions.question_text: The term "peril" in insurance means:
options: The loss itself that the insured suffers because of an event
The sum insured under the policy for the property
The cause of a loss, such as a fire or a flood
The premium that the insured has to pay for the cover

questions.question_text: The term "hazard" in insurance means:
options: The amount of the loss suffered by the insured person
The premium payable by the insured for the cover
The cause of the loss such as a fire, flood or theft
A condition that increases the chance or severity of a loss

questions.question_text: Moral hazard refers to:
options: The physical condition of the property that increases the chance of a loss
The error of an agent that increases the premium
The chance of a natural disaster that increases the loss
The dishonesty or carelessness of the insured that increases the chance of a loss

questions.question_text: Insurance fraud, such as a false claim for a vehicle theft, is:
options: A criminal offence that can lead to rejection of the claim and prosecution
A right which every policyholder has under the Insurance Act
A normal business practice that is allowed by the insurers
A way of earning a bonus on the policy of the insured

questions.question_text: Microinsurance in India is designed for:
options: High-net-worth individuals with large covers
Foreign companies with large covers
Government departments with large premiums
Low-income households with low premiums and a small cover

questions.question_text: The Bima Sugam platform is proposed to be:
options: A pension fund for the farmers of the country
A stock exchange for the listing of insurance companies
A single digital marketplace for buying and servicing insurance
A bank that serves the insurance agents of the country

questions.question_text: "Insurance for all by 2047" is a goal that aims at:
options: Providing every citizen with a free house in a city or a village
Providing every citizen with a pension on retirement from work
Providing every citizen with a suitable life, health and property cover
Providing every citizen with a bank loan for buying a house

questions.question_text: The most important thing to do before signing the proposal form for an insurance policy is to:
options: Ask the agent to fill in the form without reading it
Read the terms, disclose the facts correctly and check the exclusions
Sign it quickly as the agent says it is a formality
Leave the health questions blank so that the premium is low
